title: Button rules follow Apple HIG by role, with glass limited to floating controls
context: Decision 0113 fixed the touch target and placement rules but left list rows on `wide`, kept `sm` and `xs` sizes under 44px, and left the recording panel and chips open. Header, back and close controls were 32px and each page picked its own button size, below HIG's 44pt minimum.
decision: Button sizes are `default`, `lg` and `icon` only, each 44px tall under `pointer: coarse` and 36, 40 and 36x36 under `pointer: fine`; `sm`, `xs` and `wide` are removed. Size follows role: a page's primary action and every `type="submit"` use `lg`, an in-section action and AlertDialog actions use `default`, and side-by-side buttons share one size with the variant showing importance. Floating header, back and close controls alone use the outline-free `glass` variant, with RiArrowLeftSLine and RiCloseLine as their only glyphs. Single-select, immediately applied choices use the `segmented` variant, whose selected state follows `aria-pressed` or radio checked.

alternatives.reason: Dense desktop layouts need compact hit areas, hence the `pointer: fine` sizes.
They fall below the touch target and let each page pick its own size; role-based `default` and `lg` are enough.

alternatives.option: Add a lint rule for size by role
alternatives.reason: The role of a button is a semantic judgement a rule cannot decide, so a rule would produce false confidence.

consequences: Every `sm` and `xs` caller moved to `default`, and header, back, close and segmented controls moved to the shared glass and segmented variants.
The navigation FAB and the landing CTAButton keep their own sizes.
No lint enforces size rules because the role classification is a semantic judgement guarded by DESIGN.md and review.
Dialog header controls and page layouts were re-checked at the 44px size.
Decision 0113 is superseded; its still-valid rules are restated here.
revisitTriggers: A role appears that neither `default` nor `lg` fits.
